outcomes.text: You win. Chief loses face in front of 300 guests and one videographer. He will remember your face.

beats.text: 'I'm coming with my friends.' She came with five. A VIP lounge on Ozumba Mbadiwe. Ivie has ordered two bottles already.
So you're the one paying? Lovely. Waiter! The big sparkler!
{tell}

chief_sponsor.text: Ivie, loudly: 'Enjoy her tonight. From Friday, she's booked till Monday.' Mercy throws a napkin at her.

japa.text: Ivie raises her glass: 'To Mercy's last Lagos summer!' Mercy: 'She's drunk. Ignore her.'

quitting.text: The waiter leans in: 'Madam, Daddy Lekki says the table is on him.' Mercy: 'Tell him no. Tell him NO.'

choices.label: Pay the whole bill. ₦180k. Be a legend.
choices.broke_text: Your account left the lounge before you did.
choices.receipt: You paid for Mercy and five friends.

outcomes.text: Ivie declares you family. Mercy is a little embarrassed and a lot impressed.

choices.label: "Me and Mercy are paid. Friends, una well done."
choices.receipt: You paid only for yourself and Mercy.

outcomes.text: Silence. Then Ivie laughs: 'Okay, accountant.' Mercy is laughing hardest.

choices.label: "Enjoy, ladies!" Walk out before the bill.
choices.receipt: You walked out before the bill came.

outcomes.text: Mercy follows you out, laughing. 'You're mad. I like mad.' Ivie pays. Ivie always has money.
The bill comes to Mercy. She pays it. She doesn't call you for a day.

choices.label: "Skip the bottles. Suya run. My treat."
choices.receipt: You swapped bottle service for a suya run.

outcomes.text: Six women on a kerb at 2am, eating suya off newspaper. Mercy: 'Best night I've had in a year.' She means it.

choices.label: Ask Ivie, quietly, what Mercy isn't telling you
choices.receipt: You asked Ivie what Mercy wasn't telling you.

outcomes.text: Ivie: 'Ask her yourself.' Ivie physically cannot lie, so she just doesn't answer.

chief_sponsor.text: Ivie whispers: 'There's a Chief. Red cap. He pays her rent and owns her Fridays.'

japa.text: Ivie: 'She's going. Canada. Soon. You didn't hear it from me.' You did, though.

quitting.text: Ivie: 'She's leaving all of them for you. Don't you dare waste it.'

choices.label: [Runs] Fake a card decline. Vanish in the confusion.
choices.receipt: You faked a card decline to escape the bill.

outcomes.text: Clean exit. Mercy texts: 'Thief 😂. Respect.'
Ivie catches you at the door. Ivie always catches people at the door.

beats.text: Mercy is live, selling bags. 4,000 viewers. She pulls you into frame without warning.
Everybody, say hi to my person! Person, tell them this bag is original.
{tell}

chief_sponsor.text: A comment floats up from an account whose picture is a red chief's cap: 'Call me. Now.' She swipes it away.

japa.text: Every price she calls, she says twice: naira for the live, dollars under her breath.

quitting.text: A comment from 'Daddy Lekki': 'Remember who paid for that ring light.' She blocks him live, smiling.

choices.label: "Original. I swear on my village."
choices.receipt: You swore the bags were original on Mercy's live.

outcomes.text: Nine bags sold in four minutes. Off-camera, she mouths 'marry me'.
A viewer: 'I bought this same bag in Balogun yesterday for ₦9k.' Two hundred laughing emojis.

choices.label: Duck out of frame. Your face is your business.
choices.receipt: You ducked out of Mercy's live.

outcomes.text: She keeps selling, but texts you mid-live: 'Shy? Okay. I'll keep you for myself.'

choices.label: Reply to the shady comment live: "Who is this?"
choices.receipt: You fought a commenter on Mercy's live.

outcomes.text: 4,000 people watch you fight a comment. The clip outlives the bags.

choices.label: Buy the bag live to boost her numbers. ₦70k.
choices.receipt: You bought a bag on Mercy's live.

outcomes.text: 'SOLD to my person!' Orders spike. She sends you the bag with a note: 'Not original. Neither are you. Love you.'

choices.label: Buy the ₦8k keyring. Loudly.
choices.receipt: You bought a keyring on Mercy's live.

outcomes.text: 'A KEYRING!' She makes it a whole segment. Keyrings sell out.

beats.text: One week together. Ikoyi rooftop. A man in a red cap pulls out a chair at your table without asking.
Mercy. Friday is tomorrow. Why are you eating my money with somebody else?
{tell}

chief_sponsor.text: Down on Bourdillon, Musa leans on the tinted Prado. He waves at Mercy like an old colleague.

choices.label: "Mercy. Him or me. Now."
choices.receipt: You made Mercy choose between you and Chief.

outcomes.text: She takes off his bracelet and drops it in his pepper soup. 'You. I choose you.' Chief eats the soup anyway.
She looks at the table a long time. 'Give me till Monday.' Monday. Always Monday.

choices.label: Take Chief's envelope. ₦1m to disappear.
choices.receipt: You took ₦1m from Chief to disappear.

outcomes.text: He pays you to vanish. Mercy watches you count it. You both learn what you are.

choices.label: Stand up: "Everybody, meet Mercy's sponsor!"
choices.receipt: You announced Mercy's sponsor to the whole rooftop.

outcomes.text: The terrace turns. Phones rise. Chief hides behind his cap. Mercy walks out without her bag.

choices.label: Leave cash for your half. Walk out.
choices.receipt: You paid your half and walked out on Mercy and Chief.

outcomes.text: You pay for your pepper soup and take the stairs. Behind you, Mercy says your name once. You keep going.

choices.label: "C.E. on the logistics phone. Hello, C.E."
choices.receipt: You greeted Chief by his contact name.

outcomes.text: Chief blinks. Mercy laughs despite herself. 'They notice everything,' she tells him. 'Unlike you.'

choices.label: "'Wear the gold one. Musa comes at seven.'"
choices.receipt: You quoted Chief's text back to him.

outcomes.text: Chief goes grey. Mercy stares at you: 'You read my phone.' Then, at Chief: 'And you wrote it.'

choices.label: "Every Monday, Ikoyi sand. Now I know whose."
choices.receipt: You told Mercy you knew where her weekends went.

outcomes.text: Mercy closes her eyes. 'I was going to end it before I told you.' Chief laughs. 'End what?' She turns to him. 'This.'

choices.label: "At the owambe you called her 'daughter'."
choices.receipt: You reminded Chief he called Mercy his daughter.

outcomes.text: Chief has no next line. Mercy, finally: 'Daughter. Exactly. Go home to your wives, Chief.' He goes.

choices.label: "Refund what I sent your 'daughter'."
choices.receipt: You asked Chief to refund the money you sent Mercy.

outcomes.text: Chief transfers it at the table, mostly to make you leave. Mercy doesn't stop him.
'Is it my business?' Chief laughs. Mercy looks away. Your money is in a Prado somewhere.

beats.text: Her flat, half packed. Two suitcases. A Canadian study permit on the table, next to the gift you gave her.
My flight is Tuesday. I was going to tell you Monday. You were the last-- you were the best stop.
{tell}

japa.text: On top of the suitcase: the IELTS book. 'Band 8' circled in red. She got it.

choices.label: "Take me with you."
choices.receipt: You asked Mercy to take you to Canada.

outcomes.text: She stares. Then she laughs and cries at the same time. 'You're serious?' You are. She adds your name to a list.
'I can't carry anyone. I can barely carry me.' She kisses your forehead like a goodbye.

choices.label: Help her pack. Love can carry suitcases.
choices.receipt: You helped Mercy pack for Toronto.

outcomes.text: You fold her clothes till 2am. She tells you everything: Mama, the money, the fear. You stay till the cab.

choices.label: Tell her sponsors she's leaving Tuesday.
choices.receipt: You told Mercy's sponsors she was leaving.

outcomes.text: Three sponsors, one group chat. By midnight her street is full of Prados. She misses her flight. She never forgives you.

choices.label: "Safe flight, Mercy." Leave first.
choices.receipt: You said goodbye first and left.

outcomes.text: You leave before she can. It's the one thing in Lagos you got to do first.

choices.label: "My money. Is it in that suitcase?"
choices.receipt: You asked for your money back before her flight.

outcomes.text: She transfers it back in front of you. 'I was going to send it from Toronto. I swear.' You believe half.

choices.label: "I knew. I was waiting for you to say it."
choices.receipt: You told Mercy you'd known about Canada all along.

outcomes.text: She sits down on the suitcase. 'And you stayed?' 'I stayed.' Something changes in her face.

choices.label: "So that's why you asked the dollar rate."
choices.receipt: You connected the dollar rate question to her japa plan.

outcomes.text: 'Every day for a year.' She shows you the spreadsheet. Your gifts are in it, in dollars. Beside your name she wrote: 'nice one'.

choices.label: [Runs] Buy her bikes and client list. ₦150k.
choices.receipt: You bought Mercy's business and flipped it.

outcomes.text: You flip the bikes and her client list for ₦1.1m by Friday. She calls from Toronto: 'Thief. Respect.'

beats.text: Midnight. A silver Prado blocks Mercy's gate. A man in a crisp kaftan steps out with two boys.
Mercy owes me two years of rent and one explanation. And who are you?
I told you. I'm out. I returned the car.
{tell}

quitting.text: Mercy is behind you, holding your shirt the way a child holds a parent in Balogun Market.

choices.label: Stand beside her: "She said she's out."
choices.receipt: You stood beside Mercy when her ex-sponsor came.

outcomes.text: He studies you for a long time. Then he laughs and leaves. 'Lagos is small, my friend.' Mercy doesn't let go of your hand all night.

choices.label: "How much? I'll pay. Then go."
choices.broke_text: Your account said 'buy freedom with what?'
choices.receipt: You paid off Mercy's ex-sponsor.

outcomes.text: He counts it slowly. 'She's expensive.' 'She's free,' you say. Mercy hears that. She'll never forget it.

choices.label: Livestream him to the Parlour.
choices.receipt: You livestreamed Mercy's ex-sponsor at her gate.

outcomes.text: 40,000 views. He's embarrassed. So is Mercy: 'I asked you to stand with me, not to make me content.'

choices.label: Call estate security and your Bestie. Loudly.
choices.receipt: You called estate security on Mercy's ex-sponsor.

outcomes.text: Security arrives with a torch and one cane. Daddy Lekki leaves with most of his dignity. Mercy laughs, shaking.

choices.label: "This is too much wahala." Go home.
choices.receipt: You left Mercy alone with her ex-sponsor.

outcomes.text: You leave. Through the window you see her standing alone between his boys and her gate.

choices.label: "You're Daddy Lekki. The wrong-chat Daddy."
choices.receipt: You named Mercy's ex-sponsor to his face.

outcomes.text: He blinks. 'She told you?' 'Everything,' Mercy says. He has no next line. He gets back in the Prado.

choices.label: "Her weekends belong to her now."
choices.receipt: You told him Mercy's weekends were hers now.

outcomes.text: Mercy looks at you. 'You asked where I was every Monday. Now you know.' She closes the gate on him herself.

beats.text: Three phones in this house and you went through mine. Sit down. What did you find?

choices.label: "Enough." Hold her stare.
choices.receipt: You told Mercy you'd found enough.

outcomes.text: She nods slowly. 'Then you know. And you're still here. Interesting.'

good_one.text: 'You found Mama's voice notes and a man I'm leaving. Happy?' She sleeps on the couch.

choices.label: "Nothing. I'm sorry. I panicked."
choices.receipt: You apologised for going through her phone.

outcomes.text: 'Next time you panic, panic at me. Not my phone.' She puts the kettle on. Truce.

choices.label: Hand her your phone. "Fair is fair."
choices.receipt: You handed Mercy your unlocked phone.

outcomes.text: She scrolls for four seconds and hands it back. 'Your life is so boring. I love it.'

beats.text: The day after the pop-up. Merci Luxe made ₦640k. Mercy is counting it on the shop floor in her socks.
Half of this is yours. Don't argue. Or argue. I like when you argue.

choices.label: Take your half. You earned it.
choices.receipt: You took your half of the pop-up profit.

outcomes.text: She transfers it with a note: 'Shareholder dividend 😌'.

japa.text: She transfers it: 'Shareholder dividend.' Her half goes straight to a Toronto account. You see the app.

choices.label: "Reinvest it. Sign the real lease."
choices.receipt: You told Mercy to reinvest and sign the lease.

outcomes.text: She signs a one-year lease with your pen. 'One year on Admiralty Way,' she says, like a promise.

japa.text: She holds the pen over the lease. 'One year...' She doesn't sign. 'I can't promise you a year.'

chief_sponsor.text: She signs. The landlord smiles: 'Chief already paid the caution fee.' Mercy closes her eyes.

choices.label: Celebrate on the floor: suya and Fanta.
choices.receipt: You celebrated Mercy's pop-up with suya on the floor.

outcomes.text: You eat suya on the shop floor till the security man joins you. He has opinions about pricing.

beats.text: A DM from a stranger with no profile picture.
That kitchen in your story. I know those tiles. Tell Mercy I'm watching.

choices.label: "Who is this?"
choices.receipt: You asked the stranger who they were.

outcomes.text: Read. No reply. The tiles look different now.

chief_sponsor.text: A voice note: an older man, laughing. 'Ask her who paid for the tiles. 🧢'

japa.text: 'Her landlord. She gave notice for December and said she's relocating. Relocating where, abeg?'

quitting.text: 'Daddy Lekki. She owes me. Tell her to come back.' You screenshot it for her.

choices.label: Forward it to Mercy.
choices.receipt: You forwarded the stranger's DM to Mercy.

outcomes.text: She calls in ten seconds. 'Block him. Delete it. I'm coming over.' She comes over.

quitting.text: She calls, shaking. 'That's him. I'm sorry you're in it now. I'll fix it.' She arrives with banga and a plan.

chief_sponsor.text: 'Ignore him. Old client.' She sends ₦50k. 'For the inconvenience.' Inconvenience costs ₦50k now.

choices.label: Delete the story. Block. Breathe.
choices.receipt: You deleted your story and blocked the stranger.

outcomes.text: Deleted. But the screenshot is already in three group chats.

beats.text: Good morning! Mama called. She calls every Sunday at 8pm from Benin. If I don't pick, she calls the pastor. If the pastor can't find me, police. Anyway. Breakfast?

choices.label: "Sunday, 8pm: Mama's hour. Noted 😂"
choices.receipt: You noted Mama's Sunday 8pm call.

outcomes.text: 'Don't you dare call her. She'll ask for your surname and your blood group.'

choices.label: "Breakfast? Send akara money."
choices.receipt: You asked Mercy for akara money.

outcomes.text: ₦5k lands with a laughing emoji. 'Ehen. You too have started.'

choices.label: Send a heart. Go back to sleep.
choices.receipt: You sent a heart and went back to sleep.

outcomes.text: She sends a sleeping emoji back. Romance is dead. Long live romance.

beats.text: Ivie is coming out with us tonight. Warning: Ivie cannot lie. Physically. Her mouth won't let her. That's why I tell her nothing.

choices.label: "Ivie: human lie detector. Got it."
choices.receipt: You noted that Ivie can't lie.

outcomes.text: 'Exactly. So stay away from her.' Wrong thing to tell you, Mercy.

choices.label: "Is Ivie single?"
choices.receipt: You asked Mercy if Ivie was single.

outcomes.text: '...Wow.' Then 'lol'. Then nothing for an hour.

choices.label: "Tonight? Who's paying?"
choices.receipt: You asked who was paying tonight.

outcomes.text: 'You, obviously 😘'. A threat dressed as a kiss.

beats.text: Heads up, sweet: weekends I go dark. Friday 7pm to Monday. Work things. It's not you. Don't overthink it, eh?

choices.label: "Friday to Monday: dark. Noted."
choices.receipt: You noted that Mercy goes dark at weekends.

outcomes.text: 'Thank you.' Five minutes later: 'You didn't ask why.' She noticed that you noticed.

choices.label: "Which work happens only at weekends?"
choices.receipt: You asked Mercy what weekend work she does.

outcomes.text: 'Logistics.' On a Sunday. With a laughing emoji.

choices.label: "Okay sha. Send weekend money."
choices.receipt: You asked Mercy for weekend money.

outcomes.text: ₦10k. 'Enjoy your weekend.' Your weekend. Not ours.

beats.text: I passed Admiralty Way today. One day: a real store. Glass front. My name on it. No sponsors, no favours. Okay. Go back to work. I'm just talking.

choices.label: "Glass front, your name. I'm your first customer."
choices.receipt: You caught Mercy's dream of a glass-front store.

outcomes.text: 'You'll pay full price.' Then a voice note of her laughing for nine seconds straight.

choices.label: "No sponsors? Who are the sponsors?"
choices.receipt: You asked Mercy about her sponsors.

outcomes.text: 'Figure of speech.' It takes her forty seconds to type that.

choices.label: Send a thumbs up.
choices.receipt: You replied to Mercy's dream with a thumbs up.

outcomes.text: She sends one back. Romance moves fast in this industry.

beats.text: Rule: never buy me roses. Roses die. Buy me suya and a cold Fanta and I'm yours for the evening. Okay, for an hour.

choices.label: "Suya and Fanta. Never roses. Locked."
choices.receipt: You noted that Mercy wants suya, not roses.

outcomes.text: 'See? Somebody who reads.' A suya emoji. Then three.

choices.label: "Only an hour? I'm offended."
choices.receipt: You bargained for more than an hour.

outcomes.text: 'Two hours if there's extra pepper.'

choices.label: Send a rose emoji. For the chaos.
choices.receipt: You sent Mercy a rose emoji.

outcomes.text: 'Are you deaf in text?' She blocks you for eleven minutes.

beats.text: Quick one: what's the dollar rate today? Asking for a friend 😅 Anyway. Dinner tomorrow?

choices.label: "About ₦1,550. Which friend is converting?"
choices.receipt: You caught Mercy asking about the dollar rate.

outcomes.text: 'A friend. A very far friend.' Then, fast: 'Dinner?'

choices.label: "Dinner! Yes. Where?"
choices.receipt: You skipped the rate and said yes to dinner.

outcomes.text: 'Somewhere I can wear the gold dress.' She has never not had a gold dress.

choices.label: "Ask Google. I'm busy."
choices.receipt: You told Mercy to ask Google.

outcomes.text: 'Rude. Correct, but rude.'
